metadata.title: Fast convex optimization via a third-order in time evolution equation: TOGES-V an improved version of TOGES*

items.name: TOGES-V
items.statement:
$$
(\text {TOGES - V}) \dddot {u} (t) + \frac {\alpha + 7}{t} \ddot {u} (t) + \frac {5 (\alpha + 1)}{t ^ {2}} \dot {u} (t) + \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) = 0.
$$
items.remark: [Note: statement appears to use a third derivative while later algebra uses it; preserve source notation and type-check against the ODE]

items.name: TOGES
items.statement:
$$
\text {(TOGES)} \quad \ddot {u} (t) + \frac {3 \alpha + 5}{2 t} \ddot {u} (t) + \frac {3 \alpha - 1}{t ^ {2}} \dot {u} (t) + \nabla f (u (t) + t \dot {u} (t)) = 0.
$$
items.remark: [Note: source displays two second-derivative terms; compare the cited 2022 TOGES equation before formalization]

items.name: Strongly convex third-order evolution equation
items.remark: [Note: require $\mu>0$ so $\sqrt\mu$ and $1/\sqrt\mu$ are defined]

items.name: Convex differentiable objective and first-order inequality
items.statement: A differentiable function $f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R$ is convex if $f((1-s)x+sy)\leq(1-s)f(x)+sf(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal H$ and $s\in[0,1]$. For such an $f$, $f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal H$.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Convex.Basic] recall convexity infrastructure | [Prove hint: the displayed first-order inequality is the convexity fact used in (15)]

items.name: Strong convexity
items.statement: For $\mu>0$, a differentiable function $f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R$ is $\mu$-strongly convex if $f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal H$.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Operator.Linear] recall IsStronglyMonotone for the corresponding gradient property]

items.name: Convex subdifferential
items.statement: For a proper convex function $f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ and $x\in\operatorname{dom}f$, define $\partial f(x):=\{p\in\mathcal H\mid\forall y\in\mathcal H,\ f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle p,y-x\rangle\}$; set $\partial f(x)=\varnothing$ when $x\notin\operatorname{dom}f$.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.SetValued.Basic] recall SetValuedOperator and SetValuedOperator.IsMaximalMonotone | [Notation: paper writes $(I+\lambda\partial f)^{-1}$; Lean uses SetValuedOperator.inverse/resolvent]

items.name: Weak weighted Cesaro convergence
items.statement: If $v(t)\rightharpoonup v_\infty$ in a Hilbert space and $w\geq0$ is locally integrable with $W(t):=\int_{t_0}^t w(s)\,ds\to\infty$, then $\frac1{W(t)}\int_{t_0}^t w(s)v(s)\,ds\rightharpoonup v_\infty$.
items.proof: Cited from: standard weak ergodic/Cesaro convergence principle (uncited in the paper).
items.source: Standard weak convergence result (uncited in the paper).
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Hilbert.WeakConvergence] recall weak convergence infrastructure | [Note: apply with $w(t)=4t^3$]

items.name: Scalar differential comparison by integrating factors
items.statement: If $E:[t_0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and $E'(t)+aE(t)\leq b(t)$ for $a\geq0$, then $E(t)\leq e^{-a(t-t_0)}E(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^t e^{-a(t-s)}b(s)\,ds$.
items.proof: Cited from: standard Gronwall/integrating-factor inequality (uncited in the paper).
items.source: Standard differential inequality result (uncited in the paper).
items.remark: [Prove hint: multiply by $e^{at}$ and integrate]

items.name: Theorem 2.1 of Attouch, Chbani, and Riahi
items.statement:
Suppose $\alpha \geq 3$ . Then, for any trajectory of (TOGES) there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all $t \geq t_0$ ,

$$
f (u (t) + t \dot {u} (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {C}{t ^ {3}};
$$

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {1}{t} \left(t _ {0} \left(f (x (t _ {0})) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) + \frac {C}{2 t _ {0} ^ {2}}\right).
$$
items.proof: Cited from: Attouch H, Chbani Z, Riahi H. Fast convex optimization via a third-order in time evolution equation. Optimization. 2022;71(5):1275–1304.
items.source: Attouch H, Chbani Z, Riahi H. Fast convex optimization via a third-order in time evolution equation. Optimization. 2022;71(5):1275–1304.
items.remark: [Note: the paper uses this result for the rate and weak convergence of the auxiliary $v/\nu$ trajectory; its extracted statement only records rate estimates, so recover the full cited theorem before formalization]

items.name: TOGES-VH
items.remark: [Prove hint: use the chain rule for $\nabla f(v(t))$; require $f\in C^2$ and $u\in C^3$]

items.name: Lyapunov function mathcal E
items.statement:
$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathcal {E} (t) := f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \\ + \frac {1}{2} \left\| \sqrt {\mu} \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t) - x ^ {*}\right) + \dot {u} (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \ddot {u} (t) \right\| ^ {2}, \\ \end{array}
$$

and $x^{*}$ is the unique global minimizer of $f$ on $\mathcal{H}$ . To condense the formulas, we write

$$
F (t _ {0}) = f (u (t _ {0})) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \quad \text {and} \quad C = \mathcal {E} (t _ {0})   \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}}.
$$
items.remark: [Note: $x^*$ requires existence and uniqueness of a minimizer; strong convexity supplies uniqueness once existence is assumed]

items.name: Integral Jensen inequality
items.statement: If $F$ is convex, $a<b$, and $g:[a,b]\to\mathcal H$ is integrable, then $F\!\left(\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b g(s)\,ds\right)\leq\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b F(g(s))\,ds$.
items.proof: Cited from: standard integral Jensen inequality (uncited in the paper).
items.source: Standard convex analysis result (uncited in the paper).
items.remark: [Note: required for the barycentric estimates in Theorems 2.1 and 5.1]

items.name: Moreau envelope regularity and minimizers
items.statement: If $f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and $\lambda>0$, then $f_\lambda$ is convex and continuously differentiable, $\inf f_\lambda=\inf f$, $\operatorname{argmin}f_\lambda=\operatorname{argmin}f$, and $f_\lambda(x)=f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x)+\frac1{2\lambda}\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x\|^2$.
items.proof: Cited from: Attouch H, Buttazzo G, Michaille G. Variational analysis in Sobolev and BV spaces, 2nd ed., SIAM, 2014, Section 17.2.1; Bauschke H, Combettes PL. Convex analysis and monotone operator theory in Hilbert spaces, Springer, 2011; Brezis H. Operateurs maximaux monotones dans les espaces de Hilbert et equations d evolution, North Holland, 1972.

items.name: Theorem 2.1
items.statement:
Theorem 2.1: Let $u:[t_0, + \infty [\to \mathcal{H}$ be a solution trajectory of the evolution system (TOGES-V).

(a) Suppose that $\alpha \geq 3$ . Then, as $t \to +\infty$

(i) $f(u(t) + \frac{1}{4} t\dot{u}(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3});$  
(ii) $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3}).$

(b) Suppose that $\alpha > 3$ . Then, as $t \to +\infty$

(iii) $f(u(t) + \frac{1}{4} t\dot{u}(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = o(\frac{1}{t^3})$  
(iv) $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = o(\frac{1}{t^3})$ ;  
(v) the trajectory converges weakly as $t \to +\infty$ , let $u(t) \rightharpoonup u_{\infty}$ , and $u_{\infty} \in \arg\min_{\mathcal{H}} f$ .
items.proof:
Proof: To obtain (i), just replace $v(t)$ by $u(t) + \frac{1}{4}t\dot{u}(t)$ in (3). [Here the auxiliary variable is $v(t)=u(t)+\frac14t\dot u(t)$; the cited TOGES result must be invoked after verifying that the rescaled equation is exactly its hypothesis.]

To prove (ii), let us start from the relation $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t^{4}u(t)) = 4t^{3}\nu(t)$ . After integration from t to $t + h$ of this relation, we get

$$
\begin{array}{l} u (t + h) = \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} u (t) + \frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} 4 \tau^ {3} \nu (\tau)   \mathrm{d} \tau \\ = \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} u (t) + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) \frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} 4 \tau^ {3} \nu (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau \\ = \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} u (t) + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) \frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t ^ {4}} ^ {(t + h) ^ {4}} \nu (s ^ {1 / 4}) \mathrm{d} s, \\ \end{array}
$$

where the last equality comes from the change of time variable $s = \tau^{4}$ . [Indeed $ds=4\tau^3d\tau$ and $(t+h)^4-t^4=\int_t^{t+h}4\tau^3d\tau$, so the final integral is the average of $v(s^{1/4})$ over $[t^4,(t+h)^4]$.] According to the convexity of the function $F = f - \inf_{H} f$ , and using the Jensen inequality, we obtain [The coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one, and integral Jensen is applied to the probability measure $ds/((t+h)^4-t^4)$.]

$$
\begin{array}{l} F (u (t + h)) \leq \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} F (u (t)) \\ \left. + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) F \left(\frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t ^ {4}} ^ {(t + h) ^ {4}} v (s ^ {1 / 4}) \mathrm{d} s\right) \right. \\ \leq \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} F (u (t)) \\ \left. + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) \frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t ^ {4}} ^ {(t + h) ^ {4}} F \left(\nu (s ^ {1 / 4})\right) \mathrm{d} s. \right. \\ \end{array}
$$

Using again the change of time variable $s = \tau^{4}$ , we get

$$
\int_ {t ^ {4}} ^ {(t + h) ^ {4}} F (\nu (s ^ {1 / 4})) \mathrm{d} s = \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} 4 \tau^ {3} F (\nu (\tau)) \mathrm{d} \tau .
$$

It follows

$$
\begin{array}{l} F (u (t + h)) \leq \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} F (u (t)) \\ \left. + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) \frac {1}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} F (\nu (\tau)) 4 \tau^ {3} \mathrm{d} \tau .\right. \\ \end{array}
$$

Using the assertion $(i)$ , we obtain the existence of a constant $C > 0$ such that

$$
\begin{array}{l} F (u (t + h)) \leq \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} F (u (t)) + \left(1 - \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4}\right) \frac {C}{(t + h) ^ {4} - t ^ {4}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \mathrm{d} \tau \\ = \left(\frac {t}{t + h}\right) ^ {4} F (u (t)) + \frac {C h}{(t + h) ^ {4}}. \tag {4} \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac {1}{h} ((t + h) ^ {4} F (u (t + h)) - t ^ {4} F (u (t))) \leq C.
$$

By letting $h \to 0^{+}$ in the above inequality, we get [Since $u$ and $f$ are differentiable along the trajectory, $t\mapsto t^4F(u(t))$ is right differentiable; its right derivative is bounded by $C$.]

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (t ^ {4} F (u (t))) \leq C = \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (C t),
$$

which implies that $t \mapsto t^{4}F(u(t)) - Ct$ is non-increasing. Consequently,

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f = F (u (t)) \leq (t _ {0} ^ {4} F (u (t _ {0})) - C t _ {0}) \frac {1}{t ^ {4}} + \frac {C}{t ^ {3}}. \tag {5}
$$

We conclude that $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3})$ as $t \to +\infty$ .

(iii) Take now $\alpha > 3$ . We know that $\nu(t)$ converges weakly to some $\nu_{\infty} \in \arg\min_{\mathcal{H}} f$ . The relation

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (t ^ {4} u (t)) = 4 t ^ {3} v (t)
$$

gives after integration

$$
t ^ {4} u (t) = t _ {0} ^ {4} u (t _ {0}) + \int_ {t _ {0}} ^ {t} 4 \tau^ {3} \nu (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau .
$$

Equivalently,

$$
u (t) = \frac {t _ {0} ^ {4} u (t _ {0})}{t ^ {4}} + \frac {1}{t ^ {4}} \int_ {t _ {0}} ^ {t} 4 \tau^ {3} \nu (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau .
$$

Note that $\int_{t_{0}}^{t}4\tau^{3}\mathrm{d}\tau\sim t^{4}$ as $t\to+\infty$ . As a general rule, convergence implies ergodic convergence. [More precisely, apply weak weighted Cesaro convergence to $v(\tau)\rightharpoonup v_\infty$ with weight $4\tau^3$; the initial term $t_0^4u(t_0)/t^4$ tends strongly to $0$.] Therefore, $u(t)$ converges weakly to $u_{\infty}=v_{\infty}\in\arg\min_{\mathcal{H}}f$ .

Moreover, we know that

$$
f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f = o \left(\frac {1}{t ^ {3}}\right) \quad \text {as} t \rightarrow + \infty , \tag {6}
$$

which gives by a similar argument as above, as $t \to +\infty$ [For each $\varepsilon>0$, choose $T$ with $F(v(\tau))\leq\varepsilon/\tau^3$ for $\tau\geq T$ and repeat the Jensen estimate from $T$; the resulting differential inequality yields $t^3F(u(t))\to0$.]

$$
f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f = o \left(\frac {1}{t ^ {3}}\right) \quad \text {and} \quad f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f = o \left(\frac {1}{t ^ {3}}\right).
$$

This completes the proof of Theorem 2.1.
items.remark: [Prove hint: derive the weighted barycenter identity, apply integral Jensen, then use the weighted weak Cesaro lemma] | [Foundation: Foundation.Hilbert.WeakConvergence] recall weak convergence infrastructure

items.name: Theorem 5.1
items.statement:
Theorem 5.1: Suppose that $f : \mathcal{H} \to \mathbb{R}$ is $\mu$ -strongly convex for some $\mu > 0$ . Let $u(\cdot)$ be a solution trajectory of (24). Then, the following properties hold:

For all $t \geq t_0$ , we have

$$
f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \mathcal {E} (t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t - t _ {0});} \tag {25}
$$

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq (C \sqrt {\mu} t + \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}} F (t _ {0}) - C \sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}; \tag {26}
$$

$$
\left\| u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t) - x ^ {*} \right\| ^ {2} \leq \frac {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}}}{\sqrt {\mu}} \left(\sqrt {\mu} \| y \left(t _ {0}\right) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + 2 \mathcal {E} \left(t _ {0}\right) \left(t - t _ {0}\right)\right) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}; \tag {27}
$$

$$
\| u (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} \leq \frac {2}{\mu} (C \sqrt {\mu} t + \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}} F (t _ {0}) - C \sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}. \tag {28}
$$
items.proof:
Proof: (a) Set $y(t) = u(t) + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu}} \dot{u}(t)$ . Note that (24) can be equivalently written [Differentiate $y=u+\mu^{-1/2}\dot u$ twice and substitute (24): $\ddot y+2\sqrt\mu\dot y+\nabla f(y)=\mu^{-1/2}(\dddot u+3\sqrt\mu\ddot u+2\mu\dot u+\sqrt\mu\nabla f(y))=0$.]

$$
\ddot {y} (t) + 2 \sqrt {\mu} \dot {y} (t) + \nabla f (y (t)) = 0, \tag {29}
$$

and that $\mathcal{E}:[t_0, + \infty [ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ writes

$$
\mathcal {E} (t) = f (y (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f + \frac {1}{2} \| \sqrt {\mu} (y (t) - x ^ {*}) + \dot {y} (t) \| ^ {2}. \tag {30}
$$

Set $v(t) = \sqrt{\mu}(y(t) - x^{*}) + \dot{y}(t)$ . Derivation of $\mathcal{E}(\cdot)$ gives

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathcal {E} (t) = \langle \nabla f (y (t)), \dot {y} (t) \rangle + \langle v (t), \sqrt {\mu} \dot {y} (t) + \ddot {y} (t) \rangle .
$$

According to (29), we obtain

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathcal {E} (t) = \langle \nabla f (y (t)), \dot {y} (t) \rangle + \langle \sqrt {\mu} (y (t) - x ^ {*}) + \dot {y} (t), - \sqrt {\mu} \dot {y} (t) - \nabla f (y (t)) \rangle .
$$

After developing and simplification, we obtain

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathcal {E} (t) + \sqrt {\mu} \langle \nabla f (y (t)), y (t) - x ^ {*} \rangle + \mu \langle y (t) - x ^ {*}, \dot {y} (t) \rangle + \sqrt {\mu} \| \dot {y} (t) \| ^ {2} = 0.
$$

According to the strong convexity of $f$ , we have

$$
\langle \nabla f (y (t)), y (t) - x ^ {*} \rangle \geq f (y (t)) - f (x ^ {*}) + \frac {\mu}{2} \| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2}.
$$

By combining the two relations above, and using the formulation (30) of $\mathcal{E}(t)$ , we obtain [Expand $\mathcal E=f(y)-f(x^*)+\frac12(\mu\|y-x^*\|^2+2\sqrt\mu\langle y-x^*,\dot y\rangle+\|\dot y\|^2)$ and use the strong-convexity lower bound; all residual terms are nonnegative.]

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} \mathcal {E} (t) + \sqrt {\mu} \left(\mathcal {E} (t) + \frac {1}{2} \| \dot {y} \| ^ {2}\right) \leq 0.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal{E}(t) + \sqrt{\mu}\mathcal{E}(t)\leq 0$ . By integrating this differential inequality, we obtain, for all $t\geq t_0$ , [Equivalently, $(e^{\sqrt\mu t}\mathcal E(t))\prime\leq0$; integrate on $[t_0,t]$.]

$$
\mathcal {E} (t) \leq \mathcal {E} (t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t - t _ {0})}.
$$

By definition of $\mathcal{E}(t)$ and $y(t)$ , we deduce that

$$
f (y (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f = f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \mathcal {E} (t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t - t _ {0})} \tag {31}
$$

and

$$
\begin{array}{l} \| \sqrt {\mu} (y (t) - x ^ {*}) + \dot {y} (t) \| ^ {2} \\ = \left\| \sqrt {\mu} \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \dot {u} (t) - x ^ {*}\right) + \dot {u} (t) + \frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \ddot {u} (t) \right\| ^ {2} \leq 2 \mathcal {E} (t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t - t _ {0})}. \\ \end{array}
$$

(b) Set $C = \mathcal{E}(t_0)\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t_0}$ . Developing the expression above, we obtain

$$
\mu \| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + \| \dot {y} (t) \| ^ {2} + \langle \dot {y} (t), 2 \sqrt {\mu} (y (t) - x ^ {*}) \rangle \leq 2 C \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}.
$$

Note that

$$
\langle \dot {y} (t), 2 \sqrt {\mu} (y (t) - x ^ {*}) \rangle = \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (\sqrt {\mu} \| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2}).
$$

Combining the above results, we obtain

$$
\sqrt {\mu} (\sqrt {\mu} \| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2}) + \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (\sqrt {\mu} \| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2}) \leq 2 C \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}.
$$

Set $Z(t) := \sqrt{\mu} \|y(t) - x^{*}\|^{2}$ , then we have

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t} Z (t) - 2 C t) = \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t} \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} Z (t) + \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t} Z (t) - 2 C \leq 0.
$$

By integrating this differential inequality, elementary computation gives

$$
Z (t) \leq \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t - t _ {0})} Z (t _ {0}) + 2 C (t - t _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\| y (t) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} \leq \frac {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}}}{\sqrt {\mu}} (\sqrt {\mu} \| y (t _ {0}) - x ^ {*} \| ^ {2} + 2 \mathcal {E} (t _ {0}) (t - t _ {0})) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}.
$$

(c) Let us now analyse the convergence rate of values for $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f$ . We start from (31), which can be equivalently written as follows: for all $t \geq t_0$

$$
f (y (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq C \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}, \tag {32}
$$

where, we recall, $C = \mathcal{E}(t_0)\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t_0}$ . By integrating the relation $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} (\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t}u(t)) = \sqrt{\mu}\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t}y(t)$ from $t$ to $t + h$ (h is a positive parameter which is intended to go to zero), we get

$$
\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} u (t + h) = \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t} u (t) + \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau .
$$

Equivalently, $u(t + h) = \mathrm{e}^{-\sqrt{\mu}h}u(t) + \mathrm{e}^{-\sqrt{\mu}(t + h)}\int_{t}^{t + h}\sqrt{\mu}\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu}\tau}y(\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau$ .

Let us rewrite this relation in a barycentric form, which is convenient to use a convexity argument:

$$
\begin{array}{l} u (t + h) = \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h} u (t) + \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} \frac {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau \\ = \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h} u (t) + (1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}) \frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau . \tag {33} \\ \end{array}
$$

According to the convexity of the function $f - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f$ , we obtain

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (u (t + h)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h} (f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f) \\ + (1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}) (f - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f) \left(\frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau\right). \tag {34} \\ \end{array}
$$

Let us apply the Jensen inequality to majorize the last above expression. Set $s = \mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu\tau}}$ , then

$$
\int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau = \int_ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} ^ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)}} y \left(\frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \ln s\right) \mathrm{d} s
$$

Let us apply Jensen's inequality. According to the convexity of $\Psi := f - \inf_{\mathcal{H}} f$ , we get [Use the normalized Lebesgue measure on $[e^{\sqrt\mu t},e^{\sqrt\mu(t+h)}]$. TODO: verify the source typo in the displayed integrand, which should be $\Psi(\frac1{\sqrt\mu}\ln s)$ rather than $\Psi(\ln(\frac1{\sqrt\mu}\ln s))$.]

$$
\begin{array}{l} \Psi \left(\frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} y (\tau) \mathrm{d} \tau\right) \\ = \Psi \left(\frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} ^ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)}} y \left(\frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \ln s\right) \mathrm{d} s\right) \\ \leq \frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} ^ {\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)}} \Psi \left(\ln \left(\frac {1}{\sqrt {\mu}} \ln s\right)\right) \mathrm{d} s \\ = \frac {1}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} \Psi (y (\tau)) \mathrm{d} \tau . \\ \end{array}
$$

Then, inequality (34) becomes

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (u (t + h)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h} \left(f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \\ + \frac {(1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}) \sqrt {\mu}}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} (f (y (\tau)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f) \mathrm{d} \tau . \tag {35} \\ \end{array}
$$

According to the convergence rate of the values (32) which was obtained for $y$ , we get

$$
\begin{array}{l} f (u (t + h)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h} \left(f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \\ + \frac {(1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}) \sqrt {\mu}}{\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} (t + h)} - \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t}} \int_ {t} ^ {t + h} \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} \tau} C \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} \tau} \mathrm{d} \tau . \tag {36} \\ \end{array}
$$

Set $F(t) := f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}} f$ . We can rewrite equivalently (36) as

$$
F (t + h) - F (t) + (1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}) F (t) \leq C h \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t} \frac {1 - \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} h}}{\mathrm{e} ^ {h} - 1}.
$$

Note that $F$ is a $\mathcal{C}^1$ function, as a composition of such functions. Therefore, dividing by $h > 0$ , and letting $h \to 0^{+}$ in the above inequality, we get by elementary calculation

$$
F ^ {\prime} (t) + \sqrt {\mu} F (t) \leq C \sqrt {\mu} \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}. \tag {37}
$$

Equivalently, $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} (\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t}F(t) - C\sqrt{\mu} t) = \mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t}(F'(t) + F(t)) - C\sqrt{\mu}\leq 0$ . Therefore, the function $t\mapsto \mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\mu} t}F(t) - C\sqrt{\mu} t$ is non-increasing, which gives

$$
\mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t} F (t) - C \sqrt {\mu} t \leq C _ {0} := \mathrm{e} ^ {\sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}} F (t _ {0}) - C \sqrt {\mu} t _ {0}.
$$

We conclude that

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq (C \sqrt {\mu} t + C _ {0}) \mathrm{e} ^ {- \sqrt {\mu} t}.
$$

(d) Relations (27), (28) follow immediately from (25), (26) and strong convexity of $f$ . [Indeed strong convexity at the minimizer gives $f(x)-f(x^*)\geq\frac\mu2\|x-x^*\|^2$; apply it respectively to $x=y(t)$ and $x=u(t)$ and insert (25) and (26).]
items.remark: [Prove hint: transform to the damped second-order equation for $y$, use strong convexity and integrating factors]

items.name: Moreau envelope and proximal mapping
items.statement:
$$
f _ {\lambda} (x) = \min _ {\xi \in \mathcal {H}} \left\{f (\xi) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda} \| x - \xi \| ^ {2} \right\}.
$$

$$
f _ {\lambda} (x) = f (\mathrm{prox} _ {\lambda f} x) + \frac {1}{2 \lambda} \| x - \mathrm{prox} _ {\lambda f} x \| ^ {2}, \tag {38}
$$

where $\mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f}$ is the proximal mapping of index $\lambda > 0$ of $f$ . Equivalently $\mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f} = (I + \lambda \partial f)^{-1}$ is the resolvent of index $\lambda > 0$ of the subdifferential of $f$ (a maximally monotone operator).

items.name: Remark 2.2
items.statement:
Remark 2.2: Let us analyse in more detail the difference between the two dynamic systems of the third order (TOGES) and (TOGES-V). The key point is the choice of the parameter p in the relation

$$
p t ^ {p - 1} \nu (t) = \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (t ^ {p} u (t))
$$

which connects the two variables v and u. In [1], we took p = 1 and thus get $\nu(t) = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(tu(t))$ . In this case, the convergence of the values for u is only of order $\mathcal{O}(1/t)$ . In contrast, in (TOGES-V), our choice is fixed at p = 4, which allows us to increase the speed of convergence to $\mathcal{O}(1/t^{3})$ . Thus, in Theorem 2.1, we improve the results of [1, Theorem 2.1]. Indeed, under similar conditions, the convergence rate of the values $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}} f$ passes from $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^{3}})$ .
items.remark: [Note: explanatory comparison only; no separate formal theorem is required]

items.name: Theorem 3.1
items.statement:
Theorem 3.1: Let $u:[t_0, + \infty [\to \mathcal{H}$ be a solution trajectory of the evolution equation (TOGES-VH).

(i) Suppose that the parameters satisfy the following condition:

$$
\alpha > 3 \quad \text { and } \quad \beta \geq 0.
$$

Then, for all $t \geq t_1 := \frac{2\beta(\alpha - 2)}{\alpha - 3}$ ,

$$
f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {(\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1})}{4 t ^ {3}},
$$

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq (t _ {1} ^ {4} F (u (t _ {1})) - (\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1}) t _ {1}) \frac {1}{t ^ {4}} + \frac {(\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1})}{t ^ {3}},
$$

with

$$
\begin{array}{l} E (t _ {1}) = 4 (t _ {1} ^ {3} - 2 \beta t _ {1} ^ {2}) \left(f (u (t _ {1}) + \frac {1}{4} t _ {1} \dot {u} (t _ {1})) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \\ + \frac {1}{2} \| t _ {1} ^ {2} \left(\ddot {x} (t _ {1}) + \beta \nabla f (u (t _ {1}) + \frac {1}{4} t _ {1} \dot {u} (t _ {1}))\right) \\ + (\alpha + 5) t _ {1} \dot {u} (t _ {1}) + 4 \alpha (u (t _ {1}) - z) \| ^ {2}. \\ \end{array}
$$

Moreover, we have an approximate descent method in the following sense: The function $t \mapsto f(u(t)) + \frac{(\alpha - 2)E(t_1)}{3t^3}$ is non-increasing on $[t_1, +\infty[$ .

(ii) In addition, for $\beta > 0$ ,

$$
\int_ {t _ {1}} ^ {+ \infty} t ^ {4} \| \nabla f (u (t) + t \dot {u} (t)) \| ^ {2} \mathrm{d} t \leq \frac {(\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1})}{\beta}.
$$
items.proof:
Proof: Let us compute the time derivative of the energy function $E(\cdot)$ which is written as follows:

$$
E (t) := 4 t \delta (t) \left(f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) + \frac {1}{2} \| w (t) \| ^ {2}.
$$

According to the derivation chain rule, we get [This uses $\dot v(t)=\frac54\dot u(t)+\frac14t\ddot u(t)$, $\frac d{dt}f(v(t))=\langle\nabla f(v(t)),\dot v(t)\rangle$, and $\frac d{dt}\frac12\|w(t)\|^2=\langle w(t),\dot w(t)\rangle$.]

$$
\begin{array}{l} \dot {E} (t) := 4 t \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \dot {\nu} (t) \rangle + 4 (\delta (t) \\ + t \dot {\delta} (t)) \left(f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) + \langle w (t), \dot {w} (t) \rangle . \tag {13} \\ \end{array}
$$

Let us compute $\dot{w}(t)$ .

$$
\begin{array}{l} \dot {w} (t) = t ^ {2} \left(\ddot {\ddot {u}} (t) + \beta \nabla^ {2} f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) \left(\frac {5}{4} \dot {u} (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \ddot {u} (t)\right)\right) \\ \left. + 2 t \left(\ddot {u} (t) + \beta \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right)\right)\right. \\ + (\alpha + 5) (t \ddot {u} (t) + \dot {u} (t)) + 4 \alpha \dot {u} (t) \\ = \left(t ^ {2} \ddot {u} (t) + (\alpha + 7) t \ddot {u} (t) + 5 (\alpha + 1) \dot {u} (t) \right. \\ \left. + t ^ {2} \beta \nabla^ {2} f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) \left(\frac {5}{4} \dot {u} (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \ddot {u} (t)\right)\right) \\ + 2 t \beta \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) \\ = - t ^ {2} \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) + 2 t \beta \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) = - \delta (t) \nabla f (\nu (t)), \\ \end{array}
$$

where the two last inequalities follow from the Equation (TOGES-VH) and the definition of $v(\cdot)$ . Let us give an equivalent formulation of $w(t)$ using $v(t)$ . This will be useful for the rest of the proof. According to the definition of $v(t)$ , we have $t\ddot{u}(t) = 4\dot{v}(t) - 5\dot{u}(t)$ . This gives

$$
\begin{array}{l} w (t) = t ^ {2} \left(\ddot {u} (t) + \beta \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right)\right) + (\alpha + 5) t \dot {u} (t) + 4 \alpha (u (t) - z) \\ = t (4 \dot {v} (t) - 5 \dot {u} (t)) + t ^ {2} \beta \nabla f (v (t)) + (\alpha + 5) t \dot {u} (t) + 4 \alpha (u (t) - z) \\ = 4 t \dot {v} (t) + t ^ {2} \beta \nabla f (v (t)) + \alpha (t \dot {u} (t) + 4 u (t)) - 4 \alpha z \\ = 4 t \dot {\nu} (t) + t ^ {2} \beta \nabla f (\nu (t)) + 4 \alpha (\nu (t) - z). \tag {14} \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{array}{l} \langle \dot {w} (t), w (t) \rangle = - \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), 4 t \dot {\nu} (t) + t ^ {2} \beta \nabla f (\nu (t)) + 4 \alpha (\nu (t) - z) \rangle \\ = - \beta t ^ {2} \delta (t) \| \nabla f (\nu (t)) \| ^ {2} - 4 t \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \dot {\nu} (t) \rangle \\ - 4 \alpha \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \nu (t) - z \rangle \\ \leq - \beta t ^ {2} \delta (t) \| \nabla f (\nu (t)) \| ^ {2} - 4 t \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \dot {\nu} (t) \rangle \\ + 4 \alpha \delta (t) (f (z) - f (\nu (t)), \tag {15} \\ \end{array}
$$

where the last inequality follows from the convexity of $f$ . [Take $x=v(t)$ and $y=z$ in $f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle$, and use $f(z)=\inf_{\mathcal H}f$.] Combining (13) with (15), we obtain

$$
\begin{array}{l} \dot {E} (t) \leq 4 t \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \dot {\nu} (t) \rangle + 4 (\delta (t) + t \dot {\delta} (t)) (f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f) \\ \begin{array}{r} - \beta t ^ {2} \delta (t) \| \nabla f (\nu (t)) \| ^ {2} - 4 t \delta (t) \langle \nabla f (\nu (t)), \dot {\nu} (t) \rangle + 4 \alpha \delta (t) (f (z) - f (\nu (t))). \end{array} \tag {16} \\ \end{array}
$$

After simplification, we get [The terms $4t\delta\langle\nabla f,\dot v\rangle$ cancel, and $f(z)-f(v)=-(f(v)-\inf f)$; collecting the remaining value terms gives $4((\alpha-1)\delta-t\dot\delta)(f(v)-\inf f)$.]

$$
\dot {E} (t) + \beta t ^ {2} \delta (t) \| \nabla f (\nu (t)) \| ^ {2} + 4 ((\alpha - 1) \delta (t) - t \dot {\delta} (t)) \left(f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \leq 0. \tag {17}
$$

According to the definition of $\delta(\cdot)$

$$
\begin{array}{l} (\alpha - 1) \delta (t) - t \dot {\delta} (t) = (\alpha - 1) (t ^ {2} - 2 \beta t) - t (2 t - 2 \beta) \\ = (\alpha - 3) t ^ {2} - 2 \beta t (\alpha - 2). \\ \end{array}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\dot {E} (t) + \beta t ^ {2} \delta (t) \| \nabla f (\nu (t)) \| ^ {2} + 4 ((\alpha - 3) t ^ {2} - 2 \beta t (\alpha - 2)) \left(f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \leq 0. \tag {18}
$$

For $\alpha > 3$ and $t \geq t_1 = \frac{2\beta(\alpha - 2)}{\alpha - 3}$ (i.e. $t$ sufficiently large), we have $\dot{E}(t) \leq 0$ . So, for all $t \geq t_1$ we have $E(t) \leq E(t_1)$ , which by definition of $E(\cdot)$ gives

$$
4 t ^ {3} \left(1 - \frac {2 \beta}{t}\right) \left(f (\nu (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) \leq E (t _ {1}).
$$

Note that for $t \geq t_1$ we have $1 - \frac{2\beta}{t} \geq \frac{1}{\alpha - 2}$ . Therefore, for $t \geq t_1$ ,

$$
f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {(\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1})}{4 t ^ {3}}.
$$

Moreover, by integrating (17), we obtain

$$
\beta \int_ {t _ {1}} ^ {+ \infty} t ^ {2} \delta (t) \left\| \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) \right\| ^ {2} \mathrm{d} t \leq E (t _ {1}).
$$

By a calculation similar to the one above, we obtain [For $t\geq t_1$, $\delta(t)=t^2(1-2\beta/t)\geq t^2/(\alpha-2)$, so $t^2\delta(t)\geq t^4/(\alpha-2)$; substitute this lower bound in the preceding integral inequality.]

$$
\int_ {t _ {1}} ^ {+ \infty} t ^ {4} \left\| \nabla f \left(u (t) + \frac {1}{4} t \dot {u} (t)\right) \right\| ^ {2} \mathrm{d} t \leq \frac {(\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1})}{\beta}. \tag {19}
$$

Then, to pass from estimates on $y(t)$ to estimates on $x(t)$ , we proceed as in Theorem 2.1. Precisely, define $C = (\alpha - 2)E(t_1)$ , and set $F = f - \inf f$ . According to (i), we obtained $t^3 F(\nu(t)) \leq \frac{1}{4} C$ .

On the basis of Jensen's inequality, we obtained the proof of Theorem 2.1 that

$$
\frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (t ^ {4} F (u (t))) \leq 4 \sup _ {t} t ^ {3} F (\nu (t) \leq C = (\alpha - 2) E (t _ {1}). \tag {20}
$$

This implies that $t \mapsto t^4 F(u(t)) - Ct$ is non-increasing on $[t_1, +\infty[$ . Consequently,

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq (t _ {1} ^ {4} F (u (t _ {1})) - C t _ {1}) \frac {1}{t ^ {4}} + \frac {C}{t ^ {3}}. \tag {21}
$$

We conclude that $f(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3})$ as $t \to +\infty$ . Let us return to (20). We have

$$
t ^ {4} \frac {\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t} (F (u (t))) + 4 t ^ {3} F (u (t)) \leq C.
$$

Since $F(u(t)) \geq 0$ , we get $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(F(u(t))) \leq \frac{C}{t^4}$ . Equivalently $\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(F(u(t)) + \frac{C}{3t^3}) \leq 0$ . Therefore, $t \mapsto f(u(t)) + \frac{(\alpha - 2)E(t_1)}{3t^3}$ is non-increasing on $[t_1, +\infty[$ .
items.remark: [Prove hint: differentiate $E$, substitute TOGES-VH into $\dot w$, use the convex first-order inequality, then integrate]

items.name: TOGES-VR
items.remark: [Note: $∇f_\lambda$ requires the Moreau regularity result and $\lambda>0$]

items.name: Theorem 6.1
items.statement:
Theorem 6.1: Let $f:\mathcal{H}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ be a convex lower semicontinuous and proper function such that $\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathcal{H}}f\neq\emptyset$ . Let us fix $\lambda>0$ . Let $u:[t_{0},+\infty[\to\mathcal{H}$ be a solution trajectory of the evolution system (TOGES-VR).

(a) Suppose that $\alpha \geq 3$ . Then, as $t \to +\infty$

(i) $f_{\lambda}(u(t) + \frac{1}{4}t\dot{u}(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^{3}}); \quad f(\text{prox}_{\lambda f}(u(t) + \frac{1}{4}t\dot{u}(t))) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^{3}}).$  
(ii) $f_{\lambda}(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3});f(\mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f}u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{t^3}).$

(b) Suppose that $\alpha > 3$ . Then, as $t \to +\infty$

(iii) $f_{\lambda}(u(t)+\frac{1}{4}t\dot{u}(t))- \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f=o(\frac{1}{t^{3}}); \quad f(\text{prox}_{\lambda f}(u(t)+\frac{1}{4}t\dot{u}(t)))-\inf_{\mathcal{H}}f=o(\frac{1}{t^{3}}).$  
(iv) $f_{\lambda}(u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = o(\frac{1}{t^3});f(\mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f}u(t)) - \inf_{\mathcal{H}}f = o(\frac{1}{t^3}).$  
(v) the trajectory converges weakly as $t \to +\infty$ , let $u(t) \rightharpoonup u_{\infty}$ , and $u_{\infty} \in \arg\min_{\mathcal{H}} f$ .
items.proof:
Proof: The proof consists in replacing $f$ by $f_{\lambda}$ in Theorem 2.1, and in using the property

$$
f _ {\lambda} (x) \geq f (\mathrm{prox} _ {\lambda f} x), \tag {39}
$$

which is a direct consequence of the definition (38) of the proximal mapping. [From (38), $f_\lambda(x)=f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x)+\frac1{2\lambda}\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x\|^2$, and the final term is nonnegative because $\lambda>0$. The Moreau regularity theorem supplies the convex $C^1$ hypotheses and equality of infima/minimizers needed to invoke Theorem 2.1.]
items.remark: [Prove hint: apply Theorem 2.1 to $f_\lambda$, then use $f_\lambda(x)\ge f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x)$]

external_theorems.name: Weak weighted Cesaro convergence
external_theorems.statement: If $v(t)\rightharpoonup v_\infty$ in a Hilbert space and $w\geq0$ is locally integrable with $W(t):=\int_{t_0}^t w(s)\,ds\to\infty$, then $\frac1{W(t)}\int_{t_0}^t w(s)v(s)\,ds\rightharpoonup v_\infty$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: standard weak ergodic/Cesaro convergence principle (uncited in the paper).
external_theorems.source: Standard weak convergence result (uncited in the paper).
external_theorems.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Hilbert.WeakConvergence] recall weak convergence infrastructure | [Note: apply with $w(t)=4t^3$]

external_theorems.name: Scalar differential comparison by integrating factors
external_theorems.statement: If $E:[t_0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable and $E'(t)+aE(t)\leq b(t)$ for $a\geq0$, then $E(t)\leq e^{-a(t-t_0)}E(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^t e^{-a(t-s)}b(s)\,ds$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: standard Gronwall/integrating-factor inequality (uncited in the paper).
external_theorems.source: Standard differential inequality result (uncited in the paper).

external_theorems.name: Theorem 2.1 of Attouch, Chbani, and Riahi
external_theorems.statement:
Suppose $\alpha \geq 3$ . Then, for any trajectory of (TOGES) there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all $t \geq t_0$ ,

$$
f (u (t) + t \dot {u} (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {C}{t ^ {3}};
$$

$$
f (u (t)) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f \leq \frac {1}{t} \left(t _ {0} \left(f (x (t _ {0})) - \inf _ {\mathcal {H}} f\right) + \frac {C}{2 t _ {0} ^ {2}}\right).
$$

external_theorems.statement: If $F$ is convex, $a<b$, and $g:[a,b]\to\mathcal H$ is integrable, then $F\!\left(\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b g(s)\,ds\right)\leq\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b F(g(s))\,ds$.

external_theorems.name: Moreau envelope regularity and minimizers
external_theorems.statement: If $f:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and $\lambda>0$, then $f_\lambda$ is convex and continuously differentiable, $\inf f_\lambda=\inf f$, $\operatorname{argmin}f_\lambda=\operatorname{argmin}f$, and $f_\lambda(x)=f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x)+\frac1{2\lambda}\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}x\|^2$.
